answer: Anchor each agent identity on three independent chains at once, like a marble statue set on three separate plinths: the same bond is staked on every chain and linked to verifiable work history from each. A forger who wants a fake identity must build real history and lock funds on all three, tripling the cost. If a fraud proof succeeds on any one chain, the bonds on all three are slashed together. The ivory-tower problem of trusting a single registry disappears, and a knoll of cheap clones cannot afford the multiplied stake.
